scope: Local Phoenix release ledger, restricted PostgreSQL authorization and ordinary migration compatibility.

database.startup: Fresh initdb and foreground postgres on a private Unix socket and ephemeral loopback port with synthetic fixture roles.
database.writer: ledger_runtime connected directly and had neither superuser nor BYPASSRLS.
database.cleanup: PostgreSQL exited 0, its postmaster.pid was absent, and the temporary cluster directory was removed.

observations: The ordinary reviewed migration inventory applied successfully. Tracked paths have distinct versions for managed Linux Starter (20261120000000) and the ledger (20261120000001).

After installing the authorization and artifact schema and provisioning the build writer role, both migrations returned :ok and produced both sets of relations and both schema_migrations rows in each application order. Ecto emitted its version-order warning when the optional Starter migration followed the ledger.

Under the restricted login, missing, wrong-scope, wrong-environment, mismatched credential, expired, malformed, and developer contexts had no head visibility, updated no head, and received PostgreSQL insufficient_privilege on publication insert. Fully populated settings were denied when the exact app, environment, credential, or membership was inactive or when the operator grant covered a different project.
An exact-project release_manager with the console handoff scopes published the original bytes through Releases.publish/5. Wrong app and environment were denied.
The writer could neither set recorded_at nor insert under another principal. The application rejected an overbroad recorded_at grant. Successful writes retained the database-generated timestamp.

PostgreSQL reported both same-key contenders waiting on the release head lock. One request committed, the other received :idempotency_conflict, and the head and immutable publication agreed on the winner.
Exact-byte replay, cross-environment artifact binding, uint64 sequence handling, and deferred-failure rollback passed.
integration_boundary: The SQL guard rechecks live authorization records. Caller identity admission, signed assignment verification, HTTP handling and transaction-artifact reads are composed by the owning integration lane.
